title: Negative oracle call preserves semantics
statement: Let $A$ be a randomized register program with $m$ registers and $d$ oracle deciders, let $x$ be a bit string, $G$ a guard on configurations, and $p\in\mathbb{Q}$. Suppose the instruction at state $l$ is a deterministic call to decider $j$ in whole-input mode, using register $r$, with successor states $l_1$ for a positive answer and $l_0$ for a negative answer. If $(l,v,\mathrm{none})$ satisfies $G$, the oracle answers negatively on the paired input consisting of $x$ and the binary representation of the value in register $r$, and the configuration $(l_0,v,\mathrm{none})$ has probabilistic semantics $p$, then $(l,v,\mathrm{none})$ also has probabilistic semantics $p$.
hypotheses_covered: The instruction at state $l$ is the specified deterministic whole-input call using register $r$, with successors $l_1$ and $l_0$.
The oracle returns false on the encoding of $x$ paired with the binary representation of $v(r)$.
